Hi Alicia — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Quick recap and answers below; I copied the infra Qs into bullets for your review and next steps at the bottom.

Recap of deployment modes:
- Hosted API: multi-tenant, fastest onboarding, automatic routing and prefix/KV caching. Good for variable workloads and lower operational overhead.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for your org only. Predictable throughput and isolation from other tenants.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full control over network and hardware; typically for regulated workloads or strict data residency.

On noisy neighbor / isolation:
- Shared (Hosted API) mitigations: continuous batching with fairness policies, dynamic throttles, adaptive routing to avoid overloaded workers, and per-customer priority queues. These reduce but do not eliminate interference in extreme burst scenarios.
- Guaranteed isolation: Dedicated capacity provides strict isolation at the worker/pool level. We surface per-pool SLOs (throughput and p95/p99 latency) and can set capacity reservations for critical routes.

SLO and SLA notes:
- Hosted API: best-effort latency targets, with documented profiles per model. Not SLA-backed for latency (we do have overall availability SLAs).
- Dedicated: SLA-backed uptime and agreed latency targets per route/model. We can include an outage credit policy in the contract.

Attachments: I attached our SLO matrix that shows typical latency bands and suggested thresholds for Hosted vs Dedicated. Also included a short note on isolation boundaries.

Next steps (what would help us recommend):
1) Share 1-week peak QPS and request size distribution (tokens per request).
2) Any hard latency targets at p95/p99 and recovery expectations for spikes.
3) If you want, we can schedule a 30-min infra deep-dive with our solutions engineer.

Priyom — wrote up language below you can paste back to the customer. Also attached a short note on isolation boundaries and typical cost deltas for Dedicated.

Suggested customer text:
- Isolation summary: Dedicated capacity allocates GPU pools exclusively to a single tenant. This removes cross-tenant noisy neighbor interference by ensuring your workloads run on isolated workers and dedicated KV cache instances. For Hosted API, we use dynamic routing and fairness policies plus adaptive throttling to reduce interference, but extreme multi-tenant bursts can still impact tail latency.
- SLA & SLOs: For Dedicated deployments we offer SLA-backed uptime and configurable latency targets per route. Typical latency bands we publish for Dedicated (example): p95 < 80ms, p99 < 140ms on RTX-level GPUs for common seq lengths. We can negotiate tighter latency SLOs in the contract with corresponding capacity reservations.
- Costs: Rough delta: Dedicated typically runs ~3-6x the per-token cost of Hosted (varies by model/instance type and utilization). The delta is primarily from reserved GPU capacity and not sharing amortization.
- Operational mitigations: pre-warm pools, capacity reservations for high-priority routes, and automatic fallback to a larger instance family under sustained pressure.

Attachments: dedicated-isolation-notes.pdf includes example pool layouts, KV-cache boundaries, and sample SLA clause language. Use these to fast-track their infra/security review.

Happy to hop on the call if they want the runtime engineer level detail.

- Recommendation: If your p99 target is ~120ms and you expect steady high QPS or bursty multi-tenant traffic, Dedicated capacity is the safer route. It provides pool-level isolation, configurable latency SLOs, and SLA credits.
